newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds rebound, but turnover low-key.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds rebound, but turnover low-key.

text.p: Long-dated Australian bond yields staged a marked recovery after brushing 8.0 percent in after hours trading over the weekend, but interest was fairly light given the magnitude of the rally.
"This afternoon has been far from exhilarating. If the pace doesn't pick-up we could see a soft patch both before and after the tender," said one trader.
The Treasury is holding a A$700 million two tranche tender on Tuesday, comprising A$400 million of April 2000 and A$300 million of November 2006 stocks.

A holiday in the state of Victoria dampened some of the impact of the rally, which was sparked by detail in Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report rather than the headline figures which were much stronger than expected.
A minor rise in average hourly earnings helped to offset the 339,000 leap in payrolls and dip to 5.3 percent in the unemployment rate.

Once the tender is out of the way, the main focus will switch to Australia's own labour force report on Thursday, although a preview to it will come in the shape of Tuesday's ANZ jobs advestiment series on Tuesday.

The local market's recovery saw spread differentials narrow after severely underperforming the dollar bloc late last week. However, a major spread move is seen unlikely until after the result of this week's labour force data.
